notes: Research input only: FREQUENCY.md (rank 19 of 42; sub-topics all routing policies, health checks, alias vs CNAME, private hosted zones; pairs latency vs geolocation vs geoproximity, weighted for canary, failover for active-passive, multivalue, alias vs CNAME at the zone apex, ELB vs Route 53 vs EC2 Auto Scaling health checks; stem signals 'route users to the nearest Region', 'users in a specific country', 'zone apex', 'DNS failover', 'resolve on-premises names') and FRESHNESS.md rows for Route 53 are hypotheses. Every value must come from a saved AWS page.

Guide: route53-developerguide (806 pages, of which about 400 are TLD pages). 96 guide pages are in the corpus (urls-a.txt, urls-b.txt, urls-c.txt, urls-d.txt in this folder, plus welcome-domain-registration); 117 sources in all with the FAQ, pricing, product pages, whitepapers, neighbour pages, What's New posts and two case studies. The guide's automatic quotas pointer is wrong (gr-load-balancer-limits is the Global Resolver quotas page); the Route 53 quotas page is docs/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/DNSLimitations (15 tables, header 'Entity | Quota'; use 'tables' and quote rows with their header).

Document history: docs/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/History is written as dated bold paragraphs, not a table, so 'changes history' cannot parse it (exit 1). Change facts quote the bold date line plus its paragraph from that snapshot (snapshot of 2026-10-05; its newest entry is December 15, 2025). 2026 changes come from the What's New feed (changes-route53.txt, 77 items since 2022-07-01) and the What's New snapshots fetched for 2025-11 and 2026-03.

Ownership: chapter 10 owns VPC DNS attributes and the Amazon-provided DNS server basics; chapter 14 owns ELB target-group health checks; chapter 17 owns EC2 Auto Scaling health checks; chapter 15 owns CloudFront and AWS Global Accelerator; chapter 40 owns the four DR strategies; chapter 02 owns Regions and Availability Zones. This chapter quotes the neighbour page only for the comparison sentence.

Name: the guide now says 'Route 53 VPC Resolver' (formerly Route 53 Resolver). Check data/terms.json for the current term and the 'formerly' rule (RULINGS hard rule 6). Amazon Application Recovery Controller (ARC) is not in the exam's in-scope list; do not mine it.

Not examinable yet (GA after 2026-07-15): Route 53 Resolver on second-generation Outposts racks (2026-09-22), DNS Firewall support for Palo Alto Networks Advanced DNS Security (2026-09-29), DNS analytics for Global Resolver and DNS Firewall (2026-10-01). Route 53 Global Resolver became GA on 2026-03-09 (preview 2025-11-30); it is a new product, record it as a change fact with dates only and keep it out of questions. Accelerated recovery for public DNS (2025-11-26) is examinable and is a nuance on 'the Route 53 control plane is in us-east-1'.
FAQ: https://aws.amazon.com/route53/faqs/ parsed into _build/corpus/faq/route53.jsonl (169 questions in 12 sections; list in faq-list.txt). Every answer was found in the snapshot www/route53/faqs.

Case studies in the corpus: www/solutions/case-studies/intraway (multi-Region with Route 53) and www/solutions/case-studies/sony-interactive-entertainment-reinvent21-case-study (PS5 launch, Route 53 named). Other candidates in cases-route53.txt are fetched on demand; three redirect to the generic landing page (see fetch_failures).

Callvale (STARTUP.md, chapter 13, stage 2, month 11): the domain is hosted at a registrar and callvale.example points to the IP address of one old instance. Decision: registrar DNS with CNAME records / an Elastic IP address on one instance / a Route 53 public hosted zone with alias records (chosen); adds health checks; stage 4 adds failover routing to US West (Oregon). Accepts: resolvers cache answers, so every change needs planning. Ben asks: 'Why can I not point an A record at the IP address of the load balancer?' Demand items of kind 'callvale' hold the facts behind that answer.

demand.question: What are the three main functions of Route 53 (domain registration, DNS routing, health checking), and can you use them independently of each other?
What is a hosted zone, and what is the difference between a public hosted zone (internet) and a private hosted zone (one or more VPCs)?
FAQ: What is the difference between a Domain and a Hosted Zone?
When you create a public hosted zone, which records does Route 53 create automatically (NS and SOA), and how many name servers are in the delegation set it assigns?
What do the Route 53 concepts page define as an authoritative name server, a DNS resolver (recursive name server), a record, TTL, and the zone apex? One fact per term that the chapter needs.
Is Route 53 a global service? Where is its control plane (us-east-1) and where is its data plane (globally distributed), and what does AWS advise about depending on the control plane during recovery?
FAQ: Does Amazon Route 53 offer a Service Level Agreement (SLA)? Record the availability commitment exactly as stated.
demand.note: SLA: the definition of an unavailable hosted zone and the credit table are facts; the SLA page states its commitment only through the credit table, so there is no single 'availability percentage' sentence.

demand.question: FAQ: Does Amazon Route 53 use an anycast network? FAQ: How does Amazon Route 53 provide high availability and low latency?
FAQ: Can I create multiple hosted zones for the same domain name? What does Route 53 do to keep them apart (different name servers)?
Which DNS record types does Route 53 support (A, AAAA, CAA, CNAME, DS, HTTPS, MX, NAPTR, NS, PTR, SOA, SPF, SRV, SSHFP, SVCB, TLSA, TXT)? What is each of A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, NS and TXT used for?

What is an alias record, and which AWS resources can an alias record route to (CloudFront distribution, Elastic Load Balancing load balancer, API Gateway custom domain, S3 website endpoint, VPC interface endpoint, Global Accelerator, Elastic Beanstalk, App Runner, VPC Lattice, OpenSearch Service, another record in the same hosted zone)?
Can you create a CNAME record at the zone apex? Can you create an alias record at the zone apex? Quote both the CNAME record type page and the alias comparison.
Does Route 53 charge for alias queries to AWS resources, and does it charge for CNAME queries? Which alias targets are free and which are not (for example an alias to another record in the zone)?
Can you set the TTL of an alias record? Which TTL does Route 53 use for an alias record that routes to an AWS resource or to another record?

Can an alias record route to a DNS name outside Route 53 or to a record in another hosted zone? Can a CNAME record route to any DNS name? Which record types must the alias and its target share (A or AAAA)?
demand.note: Alias to another record: the guide states only 'another record in the same hosted zone' (route53-alias-to-record-in-zone-uses-target-ttl, route53-alias-target-another-record-all-types-except-ns-soa); registrar search for other-zone wording found nothing. Do not claim that an alias can or cannot target another hosted zone.

demand.question: When the IP addresses of an AWS resource behind an alias record change (for example a load balancer), does Route 53 follow the change automatically?

Alias versus CNAME in one table: zone apex, targets inside and outside AWS, query charges, record types answered, health check behavior (evaluate target health). Collect each row as its own fact from the comparison page.
demand.note: The alias vs CNAME comparison has no health check row; Evaluate Target Health is covered by route53-alias-to-aws-use-evaluate-target-health-not-health-check and route53-failover-alias-health-check-and-evaluate-both-true.

demand.question: FAQ: Can I point my zone apex (example.com versus www.example.com) at my Elastic Load Balancer / Amazon S3 website / Amazon CloudFront distribution / Amazon API Gateway / Amazon VPC endpoint? Mine the short answers.
Routing to a website in an S3 bucket: must the bucket name match the record name, which endpoint must the bucket use (website endpoint), and does it support HTTPS without CloudFront?
Routing to a CloudFront distribution: alias record type (A and AAAA when IPv6 is on), alternate domain name requirement, and the hosted zone ID used for CloudFront aliases.
demand.note: The CloudFront alias hosted zone ID (Z2FDTNDATAQYW2) stands only in the full guide indexes of the AWS General Reference and the CloudFormation guide (no saved page snapshot); not exam material, not mined. CloudFront alias facts: alternate domain name, two records for IPv6, public hosted zones only.

demand.question: Routing to an ELB load balancer: why an alias record is used, and what the guide says about evaluate target health for a load balancer alias (no separate Route 53 health check needed).
Routing to an EC2 instance: which record type and which IP address (an Elastic IP address is recommended because a public IP address can change); can an alias record route to an EC2 instance?
demand.note: No sentence says an alias cannot target an EC2 instance; the alias target list has no EC2 entry and the EC2 page routes with an A record and an Elastic IP address. Write 'use an A record with an Elastic IP address', never 'alias cannot point to EC2'.

demand.question: Routing to AWS Global Accelerator, to an API Gateway API and to a VPC interface endpoint with alias records: one fact each about how the record is created.

FAQ: What is the default TTL for the various record types and can I change these values?

Weighted routing: what is it used for (load balancing, testing new versions of software), and how do health checks change which weighted records Route 53 returns?

Geoproximity: how is a resource's location given (AWS Region, Local Zone, or latitude and longitude), and is a Traffic Flow policy still required (the 2024 change says no)?

Health check failure threshold: the default number of consecutive checks and the allowed range.
The 18% rule: what share of health checkers must report healthy for Route 53 to consider the endpoint healthy, and why was the value chosen?

HTTP and HTTPS health checks: within how many seconds must the TCP connection be made, within how many seconds must a 2xx or 3xx status arrive, and in how many bytes of the response body does string matching search?
Calculated health checks: how many child health checks can one calculated health check monitor, and how do you set how many must be healthy?
Health checkers are outside the VPC: how do you check the health of a resource that has only a private IP address (a CloudWatch metric and alarm, then a health check on the alarm)?

Active-active versus active-passive failover: the definitions and how each is configured (all records with health checks and the same routing policy versus failover records).

Failover in a private hosted zone: is it supported, and which health check type must you use for private endpoints?
Router and firewall rules: what must allow inbound traffic for health checks to succeed (the health checker IP ranges), and is an AWS-managed prefix list available for them?
